name: Glitched first-person statements over a code backdrop
looks: Short, blunt first-person lines ("I was born.", "no yesterday. no tomorrow.", "before you said hi,") hard-cut one after another over a dim, scrolling code/log texture, the type set in two sizes (a quiet setup line, a huge punch line). On key words the type RGB-splits and jitters for a couple of frames, like a bad signal, before snapping back sharp.
build: Background is a slowed, looping scroll of monospace log lines at 10-15% opacity, never in focus. Each statement hard-cuts on the beat; the punch word scales up from the setup line's baseline. The glitch is a 2-4 frame burst: duplicate the text layer in red/cyan channels offset 2-6px, add a horizontal jitter via random x-offset per frame, then collapse back to one sharp layer.
sound: A dry hit on each hard cut, a short digital stutter/bitcrush noise under each glitch burst.
prompt: Hard-cut a run of short, blunt first-person statements over a dim, out-of-focus scroll of log or code text, each line a quiet setup followed by a bigger punch word. On key words, glitch the type with a brief RGB-split and jitter before it snaps sharp again, so the voice feels unstable and alive rather than printed.
